title: Add invocation-slice stabilizer and cross-tenant telemetry grouper
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: production slo noise and alert churn are dominated by high-cardinality invocation variance (prompt shape/tenant microbursts). This PR introduces two paired runtime/observability features: 1) invocation-slice stabilizer: deterministic slice keys derived from invocation fingerprint + prompt-shape bucketing to group similar calls for stable metric rollups and alerting; 2) cross-tenant telemetry grouper: a privacy-preserving aggregation layer that forms cohort rollups across low-volume tenants to surface signal without increasing cardinality in primary metrics. Design summary: stabilizer runs as a lightweight admission transform in the router, attaches slice_id and slice_meta tags to traces/metrics; grouper publishes cohort_ids to the metrics pipeline and writes aggregated rollups to a new metrics namespace (telemetry.cohort.*). Rollout plan: feature gate per-tenant, initial sampling on opt-in orgs, 7-day canary with synthetic traffic. Backwards compatibility: all telemetry keys are additive; existing dashboards remain unchanged. Migration: dashboards updated to point at telemetry.cohort.* panels; alerting rules using raw per-tenant p50/p95 unchanged until cohorts mature. Testing: unit tests for fingerprinting, integration tests in perf-canary, end-to-end against replaybench. Impact: reduces alert churn for long-tail tenants and stabilizes SLO noise for low-QPS paths. Implementation notes: deterministic hashing uses stable salt per-deployment; pew-tier customers can opt-out. See linked Linear items for eval criteria and success metrics.
